objective: Owner question 2026-11-16 (FOLD-TRANSFER-20261114-001#2; goals G15, G16): an agent attends to one not-all-equal knot at a time, flips one of its distinctions, and chooses which violated knot to attend to next, with memory of its earlier steps. On planted not-all-equal knot patterns large enough that exact search takes real time, compare it against plain exact search (CaDiCaL), tuned hand-written local heuristics (WalkSAT, probSAT, Novelty+), a random-move agent and its own memoryless ablation, with training charged amortized and not; headline is transfer to unseen and larger instances and to a second meeting pattern. Stop at the frozen decision rule (real win, mechanism win, clean loss or inconclusive).
title: Does a learned choice of which knot to act on next, with memory of earlier steps, cut total work where plain search is costly?
